subject: Re: VPC deployment rights, audit access & escrow-trigger questions
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordane@forgebank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@forgebank.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: VPC addendum questions + redlines attached

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We circulated the MSA and the VPC/On-Prem addendum to the legal and security teams and they returned a set of redlines and a short list of clarifying questions (attached). High-level items they flagged:

- Audit access: they want the ability to perform an annual on-site audit or a remote attest/inspection of logs and configuration.
- Escrow/continuity: language asking for an escrow-like remedy (source/config escrow or data export) if Redwood ceases supporting the private runtime or there is a catastrophic outage. They specifically asked about trigger events and whether Redwood will provide a code/config snapshot.
- License scope: clarifying whether the Order Form grants a deployment-only license or if it includes any internal development/test copies of the runtime.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard stance on these three areas and whether you can share proposed addendum language? Procurement would like to get this resolved before week of Sep 20.

Attached: ForgeBank_MSA_redlines_20260910.pdf

Jordan Ellis
Sr. Procurement Manager
ForgeBank

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordane@forgebank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VPC addendum questions + redlines attached

Jordan,

Appreciate the redlines — we reviewed them internally and there are a few items we should align on before I send formal language. Looping in our legal and platform leads (Laura + Marcus) to propose concrete wording.

Quick clarifications to help us scope the response:
1) For the audit ask, do you require on-site physical access to customer-managed infrastructure, or will a remote, authenticated log review (SFTP/secure portal with time-bound access) be sufficient?
2) For the escrow-like remedy, is ForgeBank asking for source code escrow (full runtime code), a configuration/state snapshot (customer-specific deploy artifacts + DB schema), or a documented handover plan with a one-time export?
3) For license scope, when you say "internal dev/test copies," do you mean (a) dedicated test instances hosted in customer environment, or (b) additional developer licenses for Redwood binaries to run in non-production environments?

We have a proposed addendum draft with three options for continuity remedies (DocA: configuration export + migration support; DocB: code escrow with third-party escrow agent; DocC: extended support commitment with replacement runtime deliverables). I will attach the draft and Laura will add legal redlines.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call next Tue (Sep 15) to run through the options? If you prefer to keep this email-based, we can send proposed language by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_proposed_addendum_v3.docx

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: FW: VPC addendum questions + redlines attached

Olga / Marcus,

Quick pass from legal — inline notes below and a recommended minimal-risk position for redlines. I put suggested language into redwood_proposed_addendum_v3.docx (track changes). Key points:

- Audit: we push for remote audit as standard (read-only access to logs, config, and exported telemetry) with a single on-site audit only for cause (breach/suspected data compromise). Proposed clause: customer may request a remote audit once per year; on-site requires mutual agreement and reimbursement.

- Escrow / continuity: recommend offering a configuration-and-artifact escrow plus transition services rather than full source code escrow. Code escrow introduces IP and distribution complexity. Proposed trigger events: (i) Redwood insolvency or cessation of commercial support for the deployed runtime; (ii) sustained P0 unavailability >60 days despite remediation efforts. Remedy: provide latest customer-specific deployment artifacts, release notes, and 30 days of transition support (remote) or an agreed SOW for on-site assistance.

- License scope: standard Order Form grants production deployment rights within customer infrastructure and one non-production instance for staging/testing. Any additional copies require separate addendum or license seat.

I recommend we share these three options with ForgeBank and emphasize we are willing to discuss an escrow-agent option if they can cover escrow admin fees and sign an additional escrow agreement.

Next steps: Olga, if you want, I can craft a short cover email that maps their redlines to our proposed language and notes open items for discussion.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordane@forgebank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@forgebank.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VPC addendum questions + redlines attached

Jordan — thanks for the detailed redlines and patience while we reviewed internally. Below is a summary of Redwood's proposed positions and the next steps we suggest. I've attached the proposed addendum with tracked changes.

1) Audit access
- Proposed position: annual remote audit (read-only access to logs, config, and runtime telemetry) at ForgeBank's security team's designated account. On-site audits permitted only for cause (e.g., suspicion of data compromise) and require mutual agreement plus reimbursement for travel.
- Ask: confirm whether remote log access via secure portal + IP allowlisting covers your requirements or whether ForgeBank will insist on on-site capability.

2) Continuity / escrow-like remedy
- Proposed position (preferred): configuration-and-artifact escrow. On trigger events (Redwood insolvency or sustained P0 unavailability >60 days), Redwood will provide customer-specific deployment artifacts, container images or packages used in your deployment (subject to third-party license restrictions), deployment runbooks, and 30 days of remote transition support.
- Alternative: full source code escrow via third-party agent if ForgeBank requires it — Redwood is open to this if ForgeBank agrees to escrow admin fees and a separate escrow agreement.
- Ask: which option does ForgeBank prefer (config/artifact escrow + transition support OR source code escrow)? If artifact escrow, please confirm any specific container registries or artifact locations we should include.

3) License scope
- Proposed position: Order Form grants production deployment rights for the number of instances specified in the Order Form and one non-production instance for testing/staging. Additional test/dev copies or redistribution require a separate addendum.

Next steps
- We attached the proposed addendum (redwood_proposed_addendum_v3.docx) with tracked changes mapping to your redlines.
- If acceptable, please confirm: (a) audit modality (remote vs on-site), (b) preferred continuity option, and (c) whether ForgeBank will cover escrow admin fees if source code escrow is chosen.
- We can also schedule a 30-minute call this week (Wed/Thu) to walk through open items and agree on final language.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-forgebank-vpc-addendum (covers the Order Form + addendum once agreed).

Thanks again — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

--
